EDSA corner Mapagmaha; Street, Diliman, Quezon City OPINION NO. 70 S. 2010 May 28, 2010 MANUEL A. SY, MD Municipal Vice-Mayor Manjuyod, Negros Oriental Dear Sir: This pertains to your earlier letter requesting this Department's legal opinion relative to the approval of the 2009 Appropriation Ordinance of your Municipality. Per your letter, the aforesaid 2009 Appropriation Ordinance was approved by the Majority of the Sangguniang Bayan Members of Manjuyod, Negros Oriental. You did not sign said ordinance because you said that the approval was controversial. In this regard, you posed the following queries which we quoted hereunder: "1. 2. 3. 4. As mandated in the Rules and Regulations Implementing the Local Government Code of 1991 particularly paragraph 2 of Article 414 and I quote, "The Local Chief Executive shall submit the executive budget to the Sanggunian concerned not later than the sixteenth (16th) day of October of the current year. If the Local Chief Executive fails to submit the budget within the prescribed date, he Shal! be subject to such criminal and administrative pena'ties as provided under these Rules and other applicable taws." Considering that our Local Chief Executive submitted the executive budget more than 3 months late, he can be subjetter_l to disciplinary action. Am I right? Is the appropriation ordinance deemed approved or implementable withovt the signature of the presiding officer who is the Vice Mayor on the advise from somebody that the signature of the vie mayor as the presiding officer is only ministerial and nct necessary? Is the appropriatior: ordinance for 2009 budget deemed approved and implementaNe even before it was reviewed by the Sangguniang Aside from your good office, is there any other office that is authorized to declare thet the signature of the presiding officer

to the appropriation ordinance is only ministerial and not necessary? In reply thereto, we would like to inform you that since the aforesaid 2009 Appropriation Ordinance of your Municipality has undergone the procedural process for its enactment under the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160), the same is considered valid unless declared otherwise by our courts of justice. Any issues or questions thereon as to the substantive validity and enforceability of your aforesaid 2009 Appropriation Ordinance should be threshed out by filing a special civil action for declaratory relief before the proper court in accordance with Section 1 and Section 4, Rule 63 of the Revised Rules of Court, which provide and we quote: "SECTION 1. Who may file petition - Any person interested under a deed, will, contract or other written instrument, or whose rights are affected by a statutory executive order or regulation, or ordinance may, before breach or violation thereof, bring an action in the appropriate Regional Trial Court to determine any question of construction or validity arising, and for a declaration of his rights or duties thereunder." "SECTION 4. Local Government Ordinance - Any action involving the validity of a local government ordinance, the corresponding prosecutor or attorney of the local government unit involved shall be similar'y notified and entitled to be heard. If such ordinance is alleged to be unconstitutione', the solicitor general shall be notified and entitled to be heard." Hope we have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: AT Y, JESU . DOQ Dir ctor III Legal : 20/MerJe
